<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `08ae2c1ecae5570b290094ca5cda7e8fd8c5b26c` — the merge of head `7fce4250247ba5678e817e8570bd662f93dd200d` into base `1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 08ae2c1ecae5570b290094ca5cda7e8fd8c5b26c && git checkout 08ae2c1ecae5570b290094ca5cda7e8fd8c5b26c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60 7fce4250247ba5678e817e8570bd662f93dd200d && git checkout -B drift-repro 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60 && git merge --no-ff 7fce4250247ba5678e817e8570bd662f93dd200d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `7fce4250247ba5678e817e8570bd662f93dd200d`

review (review-b, areas S2+S4) · 2026-11-15T11:50Z

I read the full diff at this head against GitHub: 4 files, +182/−32. I also read card #32620, the epic ruling 6818436831, report 6893828566 and `readHealBaseline` / `restoreArtifactRegistryView` on this tree. `check-governed-merges --pr 33825` reports NOT governed.

### Ruling conditions (6818436831)

1. **Retire the entry with `removeOverlayEntry`: met.**
   - The guard drops `boundPackageOf(packageId) !== undefined`.
   - I checked the change is no wider than the ruling. For a bound row, `readHealBaseline` lets a package-scoped refusal through only on one path:
     - the row's own package read settles a miss, so the package is a non-holder;
     - the bare read is refused;
     - the pair relation yields `bases.length !== 1`.
   - A holder's row returns its own item before any bare read. So the newly admitted case is exactly the ruled one.
   - `HEAL_BINDING_UNKNOWN` (a peer on a package-less cluster signal) still keeps the logged stop, as round 2's should-fix 2 asked.
   - At that point no row of the name is stored, because the remaining-rows branch returns first. So the bare entry the verb removes is the removed row's own, and the verb still refuses a packaged artifact.
2. **Declare kept → retired, `Clause-②: no`: met.** The body and changeset both say "entry kept → retired" with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. No export, type or key moves. `patch`.
3. **Pin on a real `SchemaRegistry`: met.**
   - The objectql describe runs `flow` and `permission`, each in both registration orders. It asserts:
     - before the delete: the row is in the bare slot, and the holder read is the 409 naming the non-holder;
     - after the delete: the bare slot is empty, the non-holder read serves nothing, each holder serves its own item, the bare read is a 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` naming both holders, and `getMetaItems` lists the two holders only.
   - An `action` control holds the package-slot path.
   - Ablation (bound-row exclusion restored, through the built dist with the preflight marker present): 5 red / 2 green, and 7/7 after restore. The discarded no-op first leg is reported honestly.
4. **Cite the ruling: met** (body line 18, and the code comments).

### Deviations judged

- **The pin sits in `packages/objectql/src/protocol-registry-heal-packageless-refusal.test.ts`, outside the claimed surface: accepted.** The ruling demands a real `SchemaRegistry`, and metadata-protocol cannot import objectql. It is the same file the Q2 pins of PR #32447 live in, and the epic seat read it there.
- **The ~6-line `slot-retired` message fold: accepted.** Without it, the package-slot types would log "No registry entry was retired" after their own slot was retired. On `main` they logged "left as it was", which was also untrue. It changes log text only, and the `action` control pins it. The changeset says so.
- **Direct dependents and the full objectql suite not run locally (verify-lock timeout): accepted as a landing condition, not a FAIL.** metadata-protocol is a shared package (#33751 §2.4), so every Test Core shard on this head must be green before arming; that is the dependents' reading. Locally: the metadata-protocol full suite, 29 objectql heal-driving files (680/680) and both typechecks are recorded.

### Flipped pin

`protocol.registry-heal-package-read.test.ts`: `tier3` goes from `[]` to `['action|NAME']`, which is the declared move. The sibling `retireAnswers: false` case pins the "No registry entry was retired" line, so the verb's answer is still what the line says (round 2's should-fix 1).

### For the seat (not this PR)

The report's out-of-scope finding, class a, is a candidate with unmeasured reach. For `dashboard` / `report` (not package-slotted), the tier-2 bare baseline read after a non-holder delete is not refused. It re-registers the item the MetadataService registered last into the bare slot: a pick between two holders, against ADR-0150 D3. It is noted, not filed. The seat should measure its reach in a real boot, or dismiss it on the record.

### Check-runs at this head (read at review time)

- 15 `success`, including `Lint · ESLint`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard`.
- 16 skipped.
- 17 still running: Build Core, Test Core 1–8/8, Type Check · workspace and consumer gates, five Lint jobs, and Live E2E UI. None had failed.
- Landing waits for all of them, and for Test Core above all, because it carries the dependents' reading.

**Author.** `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay write). The claim is 6892357189.
